overview: The whole logic of vaccination rests on the difference between meeting an antigen for the first time and meeting it again.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: The adaptive immune response generated on first exposure to a given antigen.
aspects.valueB: The faster, stronger adaptive immune response generated on any subsequent exposure to the same antigen.

aspects.label: Lag Phase Before Response
aspects.valueA: Long lag phase (days) while naive lymphocytes are activated and expanded.
aspects.valueB: Short lag phase — memory cells respond within hours to a couple of days.

aspects.label: Antibody Titer and Class
aspects.valueA: Lower peak titer; IgM predominates initially, with a later, more modest IgG rise.
aspects.valueB: Higher peak titer, and much faster; predominantly IgG (or IgA) due to memory B cells and prior class switching.

aspects.label: Cells Involved
aspects.valueB: Memory B and T lymphocytes, which have already undergone clonal selection.

aspects.label: Duration of Response
aspects.valueA: Response builds and declines over a longer timeframe.
aspects.valueB: Response is quicker to peak and often more sustained.

aspects.label: Clinical Relevance
aspects.valueA: Reflects the response after a first natural infection or first vaccine dose.
aspects.valueB: Basis for booster doses and the anamnestic response measured in serology to confirm past exposure or vaccination.
